subject: OctagonAI renewal: reserved pool runway and throughput proposal
messages:
From: Sophie Liu <sophie@octagonai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity uplift / runway ask

Hi Irene,

Renewal for our Dedicated deployment is coming up in July and we need to plan capacity. Current committed pool at Redwood is 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved). Over the last 6 months our peak QPS has risen from ~50 -> ~120 and our product roadmap expects another step increase: our internal forecast is ~360 QPS peak by end of Q4 (roughly 3x today) driven by a new multimodal feature. That maps to ~480M tokens/month (from ~130M).

Can you help with:
- Recommended reserved GPU count to cover the runway + a burst strategy for spikes
- Expected per-month costs for a 12 vs 24 month term (ballpark)
- Any throughput / latency guarantees you can include in the renewal (we care about 95p/99p tail latency for 1k token requests)

We can share a short traffic profile and some example payloads if that helps. Procurement cc'd here — they will want SOW/price to start internal approvals.

Thanks,
Sophie Liu
Head of Platform
OctagonAI

Hi all — ran a quick capacity model based on the numbers Sophie shared on our call this morning and some typical workload assumptions. Attaching the workbook (octagon_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) and a short summary below.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Avg request: 600 tokens in + 400 tokens out (1k tokens total)
- Average sequence length that impacts KV cache hit: 1k tokens for inference paths
- Effective throughput per A100-equivalent at target latency (95p < 180ms) ~ 12 QPS for 1k-token requests when serving with conservative batching and KV cache misses; with aggressive batching and good prefix reuse we see up to ~20 QPS
- Expected peak sustained QPS (customer forecast): 360
- Target headroom: 25% for spikes/failover and canary rollouts

Quick math:
- Required sustained capacity (conservative) = 360 QPS / 12 QPS per GPU = 30 GPUs
- Add 25% headroom = 38 GPUs reserved
- Suggested split: 34 GPUs in the primary reserved pool + 4 GPUs reserved as a separate burst pool (on same commitment) for short-lived spikes and A/B testing
- Autoscale burst: allow additional non-reserved capacity (on-demand) of +6 GPUs for extreme events (billed separately)

Pricing scenarios (ballpark monthly committed spend):
- 12-month term (34+4 = 38 GPUs reserved): $XXX,XXX/month (we'll put exacts in the SOW).
- 24-month term: ~12% discount to the monthly committed rate + reduced overage rates for on-demand burst.

Operational notes / guarantees:
- We can include throughput guarantees tied to committed pool size (e.g., sustained QPS below a threshold will trigger capacity investigation and priority scheduling).
- Tail latency SLOs: we propose a contractual target of 95p < 180ms and 99p < 450ms for requests <= 1,200 tokens assuming the committed pool is online and customer adheres to request size profiles.
- We recommend a 30-day canary after cutover with a performance acceptance test and a rollback/fallback plan to the previous model variant.

Attachments: octagon_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (capacity calc) and a draft SOW with the recommended pool + billing template (SOW_OctagonAI_draft.pdf).

Will follow up with a slide that breaks the numbers down by QPS buckets (1k tokens vs 512 tokens) if helpful.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A few items from procurement and platform:
- Can OctagonAI get a 20% concession on the committed rate if we sign a 24-month term instead of 12? We need to show finance the delta.
- We will need the formal SLO language (what constitutes an outage / credit) and a remediation window.
- The 99p < 450ms looks close to our needs but we also care about longer requests (up to 2k tokens); can you stress-test the model for 2k-token tails and share expected performance?
- SOC2 evidence / penetration test report and current uptime SLA for the Dedicated product.

If you can add a pricing worksheet (monthly committed cost + expected overage for the first 3 months of short-term burst usage) and a quick statement of SOC2 compliance, procurement can start a fast-track review.

Sophie

Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity uplift / runway ask

Sophie — appreciate the clear asks. Next steps and our proposed commercial path below.

Commercial proposal (high level):
- Commit: 34 GPUs reserved (A100-equivalent) in primary pool + 4 GPUs in a separate reserved burst pool (total 38 reserved)
- Autoscale: allow on-demand burst up to +6 GPUs (overtime billed at overage rate)
- Term pricing: 12-month baseline. 24-month term — we can offer a 15% concession on monthly committed rate today; to reach 20% we'd need a minor increase in committed quantity or an expanded prepayment. I'll put the exact numbers in Octagon_Pricing_v3.pdf attached.
- SLOs: include in SOW: 95p < 180ms, 99p < 450ms for requests <= 1,200 tokens. For 2k-token requests we'll provide a separate performance appendix with measured tails; Ben will run stress tests and attach results.
- Security: Redwood Dedicated is SOC2 Type II compliant; I am attaching the SOC2 summary page and our standard security addendum. Full reports available under NDA.

Operational next steps:
1) Ben to finalize stress test runs for 2k-token tails and update octagon_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (ETA: Tue 26 May).
2) I'll share a redlineable SOW and the pricing worksheet (attached: SOW_OctagonAI_draft.pdf, Octagon_Pricing_v3.pdf).
3) Procurement to confirm whether Octagon prefers a 24-month prepay vs 24-month monthly billing for the extra concession.
4) We propose a target renewal signature date: 2026-06-30 and a 30-day canary window post-cutover.

Sophie — happy to jump on a 30-min call Monday to walk procurement through the pricing worksheet if that helps.

Best,
Irene Choi
